title: New Dundee Road and Huron Road development applications
subtitle: Self-storage at 485 Huron Road, townhomes on New Dundee Road, and a referral for 86 Pinnacle Drive.
overview: The Planning and Strategic Initiatives Committee held a public meeting on four development applications. It recommended approving a self-storage use at 485 Huron Road, a 160-unit stacked townhouse development at 404-430 New Dundee Road, and a rezoning for 26 single and semi-detached homes at 448 New Dundee Road. Staff asked that the Huron Road item go to a Special Council meeting on January 29, 2024, to meet provincial Bill 109 timelines.

The 86 Pinnacle Drive proposal, a 16-unit back-to-back townhouse building in Lower Doon, was not decided. The committee referred it to the February 12, 2024 Council meeting so the ward councillor, staff and the developer can discuss building design and neighbourhood fit.

Because this is a committee, these are recommendations that Council must still adopt or change. For residents, the main effects are new housing near New Dundee Road, a planned single access point onto a regional road, and continued discussion on the Pinnacle Drive design. Detailed matters such as grading, landscaping buffers and fencing will be worked out later through site plan approval.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended adopting the Official Plan amendment and approving the zoning change to allow a warehouse self-storage use at the rear of the property {{vote:m1}}.

The committee recommended adopting the Official Plan amendment and approving the zoning change, as amended to remove the duplicate visitor parking rate, and adopting the urban design brief {{vote:m2}}.
The committee recommended approving the zoning change and endorsing the urban design brief to guide a future site plan process {{vote:m3}}.
The committee referred the proposed zoning change to the February 12, 2024 Council meeting to allow more engagement with the developer {{vote:m4}}.

debate: On 485 Huron Road, councillors noted that self-storage would create few jobs and said the city should weigh employment value when land is used this way. Others said storage is needed as housing densifies and the building could later be repurposed.

On 404-430 New Dundee Road, several councillors questioned a single entrance for 160 homes and the lack of three-bedroom units. Staff and the applicant's team relied on traffic studies reviewed by the Region and noted the Region limits access points on its roads.

A delegate from the neighbouring area raised concerns about safety, the 80 km/h speed limit, building height and notice timing. Staff said the Region plans to lower the speed limit and build a multi-use trail. Councillors said the matter would still come before Council.

On 86 Pinnacle Drive, student association and housing-supply supporters argued the project adds homes near campus. Opponents, including a heritage group, said the size, massing and rear parking lot did not fit the historic neighbourhood or its recent zoning.

Councillors also asked about parking, fencing and buffers at Pinnacle Drive. The applicant said these could be adjusted through site plan approval, and the applicant was open to a taller fence and possibly less parking.
